parent_question: Can an archived Crater regression with a linked downstream fix be completed into a failure-to-recovery causal contrast by replaying the fix under the original target compiler?

source_change.title: Check arguments of attributes where no arguments are expected

downstream_fix.change_summary: Two occurrences of #[inline(always = true)] were changed to #[inline(always)]; no other repository content changed between the reviewed base and head commits.
downstream_fix.published_source_alignment: The Rust source files in spectest-0.1.2 matched the fix PR base package source. Packaging metadata, the normalized Cargo.toml, Cargo.toml.orig and README placement were the only package-layout differences observed.

local_replay.subject: the published spectest-0.1.2 source
local_replay.intervention: apply only the two-line downstream fix to the published source

shared_conditions.lockfile: one lockfile generated with the target Cargo and copied unchanged to all arms

arms.name: target_compiler_with_published_source
arms.failure_signature: E0539: malformed inline attribute input at src/lib.rs lines 104 and 110

comparability.verdict: The three local arms isolate the compiler change and the exact downstream repair, reproduce the archived failure signature, and confirm recovery. This is a complete causal contrast for the versioned package subject, but not a byte-for-byte rerun of the original Crater environment.
fixed: original baseline and target compiler commits
one shared dependency lockfile across all local arms
fresh build target for every repetition
changed: compiler commit between the first and second arms
only the two-line downstream repair between the second and third arms
limitations: The archived experiment resolved 84 packages in April; the replay resolved 56 packages in August, so the dependency closure is not identical to the original run even though it is held constant across all replay arms.
The exact archived container image did not finish pulling during the bounded attempt, so the replay ran on the host rather than inside the original container digest.
The result establishes versioned package breakage and repair. It does not imply that the target repository default branch at the source PR cutoff was broken.

claim_update: Crater can yield high-quality causal recovery cases when the executed package version aligns with a linked downstream fix and both compiler artifacts remain available. One such case is now complete; this does not yet establish source-wide yield.
next_action: Apply the same alignment and replay protocol to the remaining four linked downstream fixes, retaining all negative and non-comparable outcomes.
